issue_request: FHIR-36700 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for R5 and asked FHIR-I to clarify ElementDefinition.pattern[x] so patterns apply to each occurrence of the constrained element, to fix confusing array wording, and to add pattern usage examples linked from the pattern[x] comment.
initial_application: The issue appears to have been applied by commit 44ed2366be24968481e1dc367d04cff3be43df0d, which changed source/datatypes/elementdefinition.xml, added detailed examples to source/elementdefinition-examples.html, and linked the pattern[x] definition to those examples. The historical commit subject used '36700' rather than 'FHIR-36700', but the content matches the Jira resolution.
additional_context: FHIR-33316 was the earlier published same-change-family issue for the pattern[x] array sentence and was applied before FHIR-36700. The linked Zulip thread and FHIR-I 2022-04-04 minutes show FHIR-36700 settled the remaining confusion: a pattern declared on a repeating element applies to all repetitions, while nested arrays recursively require at least one matching nested repetition. FHIR-28126 later added the separate optional-element qualifier, explaining the current 'if the element has a value' wording.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The latest combined branch already has the all-repetitions rule, slicing guidance for subset matching, and the examples link in the authoritative ElementDefinition spreadsheet source, and the examples page contains primitive, complex, and repeating pattern examples.
